quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #19
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Hunting area.
State park.
Deer crossing.
Wildlife preserve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Deer crossing.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that deer cross the road in this area. Slow down, stay alert, and be ready to stop.

questions.question: A steady yellow traffic light means a ____ light will appear soon.

options.text: Flashing yellow
Steady green
Steady red
Flashing red

questions.correctAnswerText: Steady red
questions.explanation: A steady yellow light means a steady red light will come next.

questions.question: "Highway hypnosis" happens when:

options.text: You stare at the road for a long time.
You take frequent rest stops.
You sleep too much the night before.
You take short trips on expressways.

questions.correctAnswerText: You stare at the road for a long time.
questions.explanation: Highway hypnosis occurs when you stare straight ahead for too long without checking your mirrors and blind spots. You stop paying attention and may not notice traffic slowing or stopping in front of you.

questions.question: Many crashes happen when:

options.text: Drivers go too fast for the conditions.
Drivers check mirrors and blind spots.
Drivers yield the right-of-way.
Drivers keep a four-second distance behind other cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers go too fast for the conditions.
questions.explanation: Many crashes are caused by drivers speeding or going too fast for road conditions. Always drive at or below the speed limit and slow down when conditions are poor.

questions.question: ____ make it take longer to stop and make crashes more severe.

options.text: High speeds
Slow speeds
Driving at night
Driving uphill

questions.correctAnswerText: High speeds
questions.explanation: High speeds increase how far you travel before stopping and make crashes more serious. The faster you drive, the greater the impact force in a collision.

questions.question: When dealing with pedestrians, a driver must:

options.text: Make sure the pedestrian sees your vehicle.
Always yield, even if the pedestrian is wrong.
Yield only when the pedestrian has the right-of-way.
Slow down and honk your horn at crosswalks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always yield, even if the pedestrian is wrong.
questions.explanation: You must do everything possible to avoid hitting a pedestrian, regardless of who is at fault. Always watch for pedestrians and yield to them, even if they are crossing illegally.

questions.question: What does a single dashed yellow line mean?

options.text: You may pass if it is safe.
Both lanes go the same direction.
You may not pass.
You may pass even if it is dangerous.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may pass if it is safe.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic going in opposite directions. A single dashed yellow line means drivers can pass in both directions if it is safe. Only pass when you won't interfere with oncoming traffic.

questions.question: A driver entering the road from a driveway or private road:

options.text: Has the right-of-way.
Should yield to drivers on the public road.
May force their way into traffic.
Can assume other drivers will move for them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should yield to drivers on the public road.
questions.explanation: When entering traffic from a driveway or private road, you must yield to all drivers already on the public road. Merge safely when it is clear.

questions.question: At a railroad crossing with no gates or lights but with a crossbuck sign, you should:

options.text: Approach carefully and cross only when you know no train is coming.
Turn down your radio to listen for a train.
Only cross when a flagger tells you it is safe.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Approach all railroad crossings carefully. Cross only when you are sure no train is coming from either direction. If a flagger is present, follow their instructions.

questions.question: An open alcohol container may legally be placed:

options.text: On the front passenger seat.
In the trunk of the vehicle.
On the dashboard.
On the back seat.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the trunk of the vehicle.
questions.explanation: It is illegal to drink alcohol in a vehicle. You cannot have open alcohol containers inside the car. Any open containers must be stored in the trunk.

questions.question: A leaky exhaust system is dangerous because it can cause:

options.text: Loss of hearing.
Pollution.
Carbon monoxide poisoning.
Poor engine performance.

questions.correctAnswerText: Carbon monoxide poisoning.
questions.explanation: The exhaust system removes gas fumes from your vehicle and keeps them out of the passenger area. To avoid carbon monoxide poisoning, fix any leaks in your exhaust system right away.

questions.question: When you see a stopped emergency vehicle with flashing lights, you must:

options.text: Slow down. If you can, change lanes so you don't drive next to the stopped emergency vehicle.
Drive to the right side of the road and stop.
Stay in your lane and keep driving at the same speed.
Speed up to pass the stopped vehicle quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down. If you can, change lanes so you don't drive next to the stopped emergency vehicle.
questions.explanation: When you see an emergency vehicle, tow truck, or roadside assistance vehicle stopped with flashing lights, you must change lanes to give it extra space. If you can't change lanes safely or there's only one lane in your direction, slow down below the speed limit and stay as far away as possible. Always slow down and be ready to stop at an emergency scene.

questions.question: Which statement about railroad crossings is true?

options.text: It is illegal to drive around lowered gates at a crossing.
You must stop at a railroad crossing when a flagger tells you to.
Not all railroad crossings have flashing red signals and gates.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: You must stop at a railroad crossing when a flagger, stop sign, or warning devices like gates or flashing lights tell you to. Not all railroad crossings have these devices. It is illegal to drive around lowered railroad crossing gates.

questions.question: Which statement is true about driving on a wet road?

options.text: As you drive faster, your tires grip the road less.
Water does not affect cars with good tires.
Deep water is safer than shallow water.
As you slow down, the road becomes more slippery.

questions.correctAnswerText: As you drive faster, your tires grip the road less.
questions.explanation: The faster you drive on a wet road, the less your tires can remove water from the surface. If you go too fast, your tires will lose grip and you will hydroplane, which means sliding on a layer of water.

questions.question: If you see an animal on the road, you should:

options.text: Do nothing special.
Honk your horn.
Pass the animal as close as possible.
Be very cautious.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be very cautious.
questions.explanation: Always be very cautious when you see an animal on the road. Drive slowly past it to avoid scaring it.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: No left turn.
Flagger ahead.
Two-way left turn.
Turn right or go straight.

questions.correctAnswerText: No left turn.
questions.explanation: Regulation signs tell drivers what they must do. This sign means left turns are not allowed.

questions.question: If your vehicle starts to skid, you should:

options.text: Turn the steering wheel too far the other way.
Turn your steering wheel toward traffic.
Turn your steering wheel in the direction the vehicle is skidding.
Let go of the steering wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your steering wheel in the direction the vehicle is skidding.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle skids, stay calm. Steer in the direction the vehicle is sliding.

questions.question: If your wheels slip off the road edge while driving, you should:

options.text: Jerk the steering wheel to force the vehicle back onto the road.
Speed up and steer back onto the road slowly.
Brake hard and stop.
Slow down gently using the brakes. Turn the steering wheel to get back on the road at a safe speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down gently using the brakes. Turn the steering wheel to get back on the road at a safe speed.
questions.explanation: If your wheels leave the road, keep them off the pavement and reduce your speed by gently braking. When you reach a safe speed, turn the steering wheel to return to the road. Do not jerk the steering wheel sharply.

questions.question: If you are in another driver's blind spot, you should:

options.text: Move forward or back so the driver can see you.
Drive at the same speed.
Stay in the blind spot.
Honk to alert them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move forward or back so the driver can see you.
questions.explanation: Do not stay in another driver's blind spot. Move ahead or drop back so they can see you.

questions.question: Signs for public recreation areas are what color?

options.text: Orange.
Red.
Green.
Brown.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brown.
questions.explanation: Brown signs show cultural sites, historical locations, and public recreation areas. They help you find these places when traveling.

questions.question: When driving near a motorcycle, you must:

options.text: Give the motorcycle a full lane to use.
Drive on the shoulder next to the motorcycle.
Let the motorcycle use only half of a lane.
Pass by sharing the same lane as the motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give the motorcycle a full lane to use.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle is a full-size vehicle with the same road rights as any other vehicle. Give motorcycles a full lane width. Even if space seems available for both vehicles in one lane, motorcycles need room to move safely.

questions.question: What color are most warning signs?

options.text: Red.
Yellow.
Green.
Blue.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yellow.
questions.explanation: Most warning signs are diamond-shaped and yellow with black letters. They alert drivers to hazards or unexpected road conditions ahead.

questions.question: Two vehicles reach an intersection at the same time with no signs or signals. Which one has the right-of-way?

options.text: The car approaching from the right.
The car approaching from the left.
The car whose driver sounds the horn first.
The car traveling the fastest.

questions.correctAnswerText: The car approaching from the right.
questions.explanation: When two vehicles reach an intersection without traffic controls, the vehicle approaching from the right has the right-of-way.

questions.question: When changing lanes, you should:

options.text: Signal before you change lanes.
Check your blind spot.
Make sure the lane is clear before moving into it.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Signal clearly before changing lanes or exiting. Look over your shoulder to check your blind spot before moving left or right. Only move into the lane when you know it is clear.

questions.question: When an emergency vehicle with siren and/or flashing lights approaches you, you must immediately:

options.text: Pull to the right and stop.
Pull to the right and slow down.
Pull to the right and turn on your four-way flashers.
Stop and let the emergency vehicle pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the right and stop.
questions.explanation: When an emergency vehicle with lights, sirens, or other warning devices approaches, drive to the right side of the road and stop.
